gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a US price for any screen next to the way it carries video. Two US prices read today show that a second screen does not have to cost more as an attached extender: ViewSonic's VA1655 single 15.6-inch portable monitor is $109.99, and ViewSonic's VG1457 dual 14-inch screen is $349.99. On macOS only one of the VG1457's two screens extends, so a MacBook owner paying for two screens gets one.
standout_why: Best Buy Canada (cited in both chats) lists about 22 portable monitors and Mobile Pixels extenders, but only in Canadian dollars. It says nothing about the video path, drivers or MacBook limits for any of them. bestusefultips (cited) explains DisplayPort Alt Mode and DisplayLink in general terms but names no product and gives no price. ViewSonic's dual-screen guide (cited) already says the VG1457 cannot extend both screens on macOS ('due to MST limitations'), so that part is not new. It also gives no prices. None of the three puts a US price for today beside each screen's video path. None checks ChatGPT's line that extenders are 'usually worse value' against the price of each added screen.
decides: For one added screen the prices back ChatGPT's pick: ViewSonic sells its 15.6-inch 1080p VA1655 portable monitor for $109.99 (read 2026-11-21). The Mobile Pixels store sells its 16-inch Glance for $151.99, and that is a partner product we could link. Every attach-to-lid extender we price costs more for a single screen; the Duex Max DS is {price:mobile-pixels-duex-max-ds}. For two added screens the prices argue against ChatGPT's 'extenders are usually worse value' claim. Two VA1655s cost $219.98 from ViewSonic. FOPO's S1 dual 14-inch is {price:fopo-s1-dual-14-inch-laptop-screen-extender} at the store and {after:fopo-s1-dual-14-inch-laptop-screen-extender} through our link with code FOPO, so it can cost less per added screen while FOPO's sale lasts. I found no end date for that sale. On a base M1, M2 or M3 MacBook, any two-screen product only adds one screen. ViewSonic says this for the VG1457 itself, and Apple's own limit says it for the rest. So for MacBook owners the honest answer is one portable monitor. For Windows laptops with video-capable USB-C, our FOPO dual extenders win the two-screen segment on price. The Trio 3 Pro (two video-capable USB-C ports or Mobile Pixels' driver) and the FOPO S788 (driver required) are three-screen setups, which the shopper did not ask about.
